sinif-ogretmeni-1.title: Classroom Management
q: How do you deal with a student who keeps talking and disrupting the lesson?
Preventive rules: rule, classroom rules, from the start
One-to-one talk: one to one, one-on-one, why, talk
Giving a role / responsibility: task, role, responsib

I make sure the class rules were set together with the students from the start. I use silent cues such as eye contact or moving closer, without stopping the lesson. After class I talk to the student one to one to understand why. I give them a task in class to channel their energy positively and reinforce good behaviour. If it continues, I work with the parents.
How do you support students who learn at different speeds in the same lesson?
Extra support: support, review, extra activit

I use differentiated instruction: students reach the same objective through activities at different levels of difficulty. I set up mixed-level groups for peer learning. Fast learners get enrichment activities, and those who struggle get extra review and support. I track progress with regular observation and short assessments.

sinif-ogretmeni-2.title: Communicating with Parents
q: A parent unhappy with their child's grade complains harshly. What do you do?
Concrete data: homework, exam, test, observ, data

I listen calmly to the parent until they finish and show that I understand their concern. I share concrete information based on the student's homework, tests and classroom observations. Together we create a support plan for school and home. I meet again a few weeks later to follow up on progress.

brans-ogretmeni-1.title: Lesson Planning
q: What goes into an effective lesson plan?
Opening / hook: opening, hook, attention, prior knowledge

First I set clear learning objectives. I open with a hook that activates students' prior knowledge. In the main part I plan activities where students are active. During the lesson I check learning with short questions. I close with a summary and suitable homework.

brans-ogretmeni-2.title: Motivation
q: How do you motivate a class with very low interest in your subject?
Link to everyday life: everyday life, real, example
Active methods: game, project, group, active
Experience of success: success, small goal, feedback

First I use a short survey or conversation to learn what interests the students and why they're disengaged. I connect topics to real-life examples. I use active methods such as gamification, projects and group work. With small, achievable goals I give them an experience of success and positive feedback.

dil-ogretmeni-1.title: Language Teaching
q: How do you develop students' speaking skills?
Safe environment: mistake, without fear, safe

With a communicative approach I give a large part of the lesson to student talk. Pair and group work increases everyone's speaking time. I create a safe environment where they're not afraid of making mistakes. Role-plays and real-life tasks let them use the language in meaningful contexts.

hemsirelik-1.title: Patient Care
q: How do you prioritize when several patients need you at the same time?
Life-threatening first: life-threatening, urgent, abc, airway, breathing
Triage logic: triage, priorit, rank, come first

First I attend to life-threatening situations; airway, breathing and circulation problems always come first. I rank the other patients by urgency. If needed I ask the team for help or delegate suitable tasks. I document everything I do accurately.
What do you pay attention to in order to prevent medication errors?
The rights of administration: right patient, right drug, right dose, right route, right time

I follow the rights of medication administration: right patient, right drug, right dose, right route, right time and right documentation. I verify the patient's identity with their wristband and check their allergy history. If I'm unsure about an order, I always ask before giving it. I document immediately after administering.

hemsirelik-2.title: Difficult Situations
q: A patient's relative is very angry about the treatment and is shouting at the staff. What do you do?
Suitable setting: separate, quiet place, quiet area

I stay calm and listen to the relative, showing that I understand their worry. I take them to a quiet area where other patients aren't affected. I explain what is within my remit and arrange for them to speak with the doctor if needed. If it turns into verbal or physical violence, I set a boundary and call security.

eczacilik-1.title: Patient Counselling
q: How do you counsel a customer asking for an over-the-counter painkiller?
Gathering information: complaint, how long, question
Current medicines / conditions: medication, chronic, pregnan
Referral: refer to a doctor, warning signs

First I ask about the complaint, how long it has lasted and how severe it is. I find out about other medicines they take, chronic conditions, pregnancy and allergies. I recommend a suitable product and explain the correct dose. If it doesn't improve in a few days or there are warning signs, I advise them to see a doctor.

eczacilik-2.title: Interactions
q: You notice a serious drug interaction on a prescription. What do you do?
Contacting the prescriber: prescriber, physician, doctor, call
Informing the patient: patient, inform, explain

First I confirm the interaction with reliable sources. Then I contact the prescribing doctor, explain the issue and suggest an alternative drug or dose change. I inform the patient about the process without alarming them. I document the change and the conversation.

fizyoterapi-1.title: Assessment
q: How do you assess a new patient who comes in with lower back pain?
Red flags: red flag, numbness, bladder
Physical examination: range of motion, muscle strength, test

First I take a detailed history: when the pain started, what it's like and how it affects daily life. I screen for red flags such as numbness or bladder control problems and refer to a doctor if any are present. I do a physical examination with range of motion, muscle strength and special tests. Based on the findings I set measurable goals and a treatment plan together with the patient.

fizyoterapi-2.title: Motivation
q: The patient isn't doing their home exercises and progress has stalled. What do you do?
Simplifying the program: short, simple, simplif
Link to goals: goal, show progress

First I try to understand why they can't do the exercises, for example barriers like time, pain or not understanding them. I shorten and simplify the program so it fits their daily routine. I give support such as videos and reminders. I boost their motivation by showing their personal goal and the progress they've made.

diyetisyen-1.title: Client Consultation
q: How do you run the first session with a new client who wants to lose weight?
Eating habits: habit, food intake, meal

First I learn their health history, medications and any conditions. I ask in detail about their meal pattern and eating habits. I take measurements such as height, weight and waist circumference. Together with the client I set sustainable, realistic goals and create a personalized plan.

sinif-ogretmeni-3.title: Leading Colleagues
q: As head of your subject group, how do you build a shared assessment standard among teachers?
Shared learning outcomes: learning outcome, outcomes

First we agree in a group meeting on the learning outcomes we will assess each term. For open-ended work we prepare a shared rubric and scoring criteria together. We share exam results across classes, compare them and discuss the reasons for any differences. We support each other’s professional development by observing one another’s lessons. Instead of imposing decisions, we make them together and hear everyone’s ideas, so the standard is accepted.

brans-ogretmeni-3.title: Raising Achievement
q: Achievement in one subject at your school has been low for years. What improvement plan do you propose?

First I study exam data by learning outcome to find the topics students struggle with most. By talking with students and teachers, I find out whether the problem is gaps in prior knowledge, motivation or the teaching method. With the subject group I plan more interactive activities and different teaching methods. I set up study sessions and peer support for students who are struggling. Short interim quizzes let me track progress and update the plan.

dil-ogretmeni-2.title: Speaking Skills
q: In an English class where students are reluctant to speak, how do you develop their speaking skills?
Pair and group work: pair, group

First I lower anxiety by creating a safe environment where mistakes are normal. Instead of speaking in front of everyone, I start with pair and small group work. I give tasks close to real life, such as giving directions or role plays. Before speaking I give a short preparation time and useful phrases. Rather than correcting errors on the spot, I give gentle feedback to the whole class after the activity.

dil-ogretmeni-3.title: Curriculum Design
q: How do you design the curriculum framework for levels A1–B2 at a language school?

I define the framework by CEFR level, with can-do statements for each level. I plan the four skills of reading, listening, speaking and writing in a balanced way. I build topics in a spiral, so structures are revisited and deepened at every level. A placement test and end-of-course exams tie assessment to the goals. I choose suitable materials and write a short guide for teachers.

hemsirelik-3.title: Charge Nursing
q: As charge nurse, you notice medication errors on the ward are rising. What do you do?
Process safeguards: double check, double-check, barcode

First I encourage errors to be reported without blame; an error that is not reported cannot be prevented. I review the reports and find the root cause, such as busy hours or drugs with similar names. For high-risk drugs I add process safeguards such as a double check and, where possible, barcode verification. I give the team a short training on medication safety. I monitor the error rate monthly and share the results with the team.

eczacilik-3.title: Running a Pharmacy
q: The pharmacy’s profitability is falling. How do you improve it?

First I review stock turnover and cut products that move slowly or are close to expiry. For income beyond prescriptions, I adjust the product mix of dermocosmetics and supplements to the local customer profile. Advice services such as blood pressure checks give customers more reasons to visit. I review expense lines such as staffing and energy to lower costs. I build loyalty by staying in closer touch with regular patients.

fizyoterapi-3.title: Clinic Quality
q: How do you measure and improve treatment outcomes in a rehabilitation clinic?

For each diagnosis group I choose validated standard scales, such as for pain and function. I take these measurements at the start and end of treatment and compare them. For groups with weaker outcomes I update treatment with evidence-based protocols. In regular case meetings the team reviews difficult cases together. Patient feedback and satisfaction surveys let me see the process through the patient’s eyes too.

diyetisyen-2.title: Client Follow-up
q: How do you approach a client whose weight loss has plateaued and whose motivation is dropping?

First I reassure the client by explaining that a plateau is a normal part of the process. We review their food and activity logs together to find habits that slipped. If needed we update the energy intake and exercise plan. To lift motivation we set small goals each week. I also make non-scale wins visible, such as waist measurement, energy and sleep.

diyetisyen-3.title: Workplace Nutrition
q: How do you set up a healthy eating program for a company canteen?

First I analyse the current menu and run a short survey on employees’ eating habits. I plan a rotating, seasonal menu that is balanced across food groups. Labels with calorie and ingredient information next to each dish make healthy choices easier. I prepare short seminars and education content for employees. I track the program regularly with satisfaction surveys and consumption data.

kurum-mulakati-1.title: Motivation
q: Why do you want to work in the public sector, and in this agency in particular?
Public service mindset: public service, citizen
Knowing the agency: agency’s mission, agency
Long-term goal: goal, long term, long-term

I see public service as a responsibility that directly touches citizens’ lives. I researched this agency’s mission and recent projects, and its work on digital services interested me most. I believe the data analysis experience I gained at university and in my internship lets me contribute in this area. In the long term my goal is to specialise in the agency and take responsibility for projects that improve service quality.

kurum-mulakati-2.title: Public Administration
q: What are the core principles of public service?

The core principles of public service are continuity, equality, adaptability and neutrality. Under the principle of continuity the service must be uninterrupted; for example, water or health services must not stop. Equality means not discriminating between the people who use the service. Adaptability means updating the service as society’s needs change. Neutrality means officials do not let their personal or political views affect their work.

kurum-mulakati-3.title: Situational Questions
q: Your superior asks you to carry out an action you believe breaks the regulations. What do you do?

First I check the relevant regulations to be sure there really is a breach. If there is, I do not carry out the order and I inform my superior of the breach respectfully. If my superior insists and repeats the order in writing, I carry it out, and the responsibility lies with the person who gave it. However, I would never carry out an order whose subject is a crime. I keep a record of the correspondence throughout.

uzman-yardimciligi-1.title: Subject Knowledge
q: What causes inflation, and how can public policy fight it?

One cause of inflation is demand-pull inflation, when total demand exceeds the economy’s capacity to produce. Another is cost-push inflation, when input prices such as energy or the exchange rate rise. The expectation that prices will rise can also make inflation stick by shaping wage and price decisions. The central bank uses monetary policy to raise interest rates, slowing demand and managing expectations. The government supports this with fiscal policy by keeping public spending disciplined.

uzman-yardimciligi-2.title: Analysis & Reports
q: Complaints about one of the agency’s services have risen. How do you prepare a report on it?

First I make the report’s purpose clear, and which period and service it covers. I collect data from the complaint records and interview the units involved and some citizens. I group the complaints by type and analyse the root cause of each group. For each finding I write actionable recommendations with a responsible unit and a timeline. I present the report in a plain structure with an executive summary, findings, recommendations and a conclusion.

uzman-yardimciligi-3.title: Thesis & Defence
q: How do you choose the topic of your expert thesis and defend it before the panel?

When choosing the topic I first check whether it answers a real need of the agency. I review the literature to make sure the topic offers an original contribution. I define my data sources and analysis method clearly at the start. At the end of the thesis I give practical recommendations the agency can use right away. In the defence I present the main findings in a short, visual presentation and prepare for the panel’s likely questions in advance.

kamu-yoneticiligi-1.title: Principles of Administration
q: What is the difference between centralised and decentralised administration?

In centralised administration, public services are run by the ministries within the single legal personality of the state. Deconcentration is a form of it, where provincial offices such as the governorship can decide on behalf of the centre. In decentralised administration, local bodies with their own legal personality, such as municipalities and special provincial administrations, provide services through their own organs. Decentralisation gives the advantage of speed and participation for local needs, while centralisation gives unity and common standards. The centre supervises local governments through administrative oversight.

kamu-yoneticiligi-2.title: Crisis Management
q: A flood has hit your district. What do you do in the first 24 hours?

My first priority is life safety; I start evacuation and search and rescue in the areas at risk. I set up a coordination centre with the disaster agency, health services, police and the municipality and assign tasks. For those affected I organise basic needs such as shelter, food, clean water and health care. I inform the public with regular announcements through official channels to stop false information. From the first hours I send damage assessment teams to the field so the aid plan is based on data.

kamu-yoneticiligi-3.title: Leadership
q: Can you give an example of how you led a public sector team with low motivation?
Listen to the causes: listen, cause

In my previous role I took over a unit where applications were delayed and the team’s motivation was low. First I met each employee one-on-one and listened to the causes of the problems. Together with the team we set a clear goal of halving waiting times. I redistributed the workload so it was fair. I recognised good work openly in meetings. As a result waiting times fell by 40% in three months and complaints dropped.
